full_judgment:
2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present opposite-parties as plaintiffs instituted the original suit for specific performance of contract being Title. Suit No.309 of 1976 in the 3rd Court of the then Munsif, Habigonj contending inter-alia that the suit property appertaining to CS. plot No.5360 of Mouza Sultan Mamudpur, JL No.17, Chowdhury Bazar, Habigonj town originally belonged to the defendant No.4 Bipin Behari Das and his brother Banka Chandra Behari Das as joint Hindu property. Banka Chandra died leaving the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 as sons and the defendant No.3 as widow. The defendant Nos.l-3 and 4 entered into a contract for sale in respect of the land under plot No.5360 of khatian No.1317 in favour of the plaintiffs at a consideration of Tk. 5,000/-(five thousand). Accordingly; in the month of June, 1970 the defendant Nos.1, 2 and 3 accepted Tk.1550/- as earnest Money and the defendant No.4 took a sum of Tk.1550/- as earnest money for their respective saham in the premises but due to the absence of income tax clearance certificate the kabla deed could not be executed and registered. The defendant No.4 receiving balance consideration amount of Tk.1000/-(one thousand) executed and registered kabla deed in favour of the plaintiffs on 04.04.1973 in respect of his share but the defendant Nos.1, 2 and 3 did not execute and register the kabla deed and meanwhile the war of liberation in the year of 1971 was started. The plaintiffs requested the defendant Nos.1-3 to execute & register the deed after taking the balance amount but the defendants denied. Thereafter the plaintiffs filed the original suit. 

 3. Vis-a-vis; the contrary case of the defendants who are the petitioners of this revisional application in short is thus, that they never entered into any contract for sale of the suit land with the plaintiffs for transfer of the suit property which is the homestead land and structure of the defendants and they never accepted Tk. 1550/- as earnest money. There was no contract between the parties in respect of the disputed property but the plaintiffs with an ill motive to grab the property filed the suit on false allegation. The further case of the defendants is such that they filed a pre-emption Miscellaneous Case being No.145 of 1973 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 against the kabla deed dated 04.04.1973 executed by the defendant No.4 and to defeat pre-emption the plaintiffs on the basis of a false oral contract filed the suit for specific performance of contract which is liable to be dismissed. 

 8. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned lower appellate court during disposal of the appeal committed gross illegality and irregularity and the impugned judgment and decree is not based upon evidence on records rather it was given on surmise and conjecture without rebutting the positive findings and decision of the trial court on the pertinent matter in issue of the suit which is on the alleged oral contract between the parties. The learned Advocate further submits that the lower appellate court has miserably failed to assess the evidence on record in its true perspective and also failed to appreciate the actual position of law and thereby committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate also submits that the appellate court below misconstrued the income tax clearance certificate marked as exhibit-1 which does not attract the disputed property and in this context the findings and decision of the trial court not at all rebutted by the appellate court below adverting evidence. None of the witnesses as adduced from the side of the plaintiffs has been able to prove the basis of the plaintiff's claim i.e. the oral contract between the parties. In spite of that the learned appellate court below misdirecting himself decreed the suit illegally which is perverse in the eye of law. The learned Advocate during hearing of the revisional application after filing a supplementary affidavit argued that the plaintiffs to the suit in their pleadings clearly stated that they have been possessing the suit premises on the basis of tenancy under the defendant Nos.1-3 and the defendants also admitted the fact that the plaintiffs are their tenants in the Premises and the relationship between the plaintiffs and the defendants is land lord-varatia. The learned Advocate also submits that,' it is the settled principle of law that a tenant cannot set up a third case in which he is monthly tenant without surrendering possession to his land-lord, which is not at all considered by the lower appellate court and thereby committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the learned Sub-ordinate Judge scanning the evidence of the PWs. and DWs. should have arrived at a decision as to whether the alleged oral contract is proved on offering the earnest money and acceptance of the same for the suit premises while the learned trial court in his observation and findings relying upon the evidence on records and on critical analysis of the evidence clearly held that the oral contract as alleged from the side of the plaintiffs not at all proved rather disproved and the pleadings of the plaintiffs has been falsified by their own witnesses which is not rebutted by the lower appellate court and as such there has been gross illegality in passing the impugned judgment and decree. 

 9. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite-parties opposing the Rule submits that the appellate court below in passing the impugned judgment and decree committed no illegality or irregularity. There has been no mis-reading or non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts in deciding the fate of the appeal. The learned Advocate further submits that admittedly one of the owner of the schedule property the defendant No.4 in respect of his particular share executed and registered a sale deed in favour of the plaintiffs and against that deed the defendant Nos.l-3 filed a pre-emption Miscellaneous case being No.145 of 1973 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The said kabla deed was registered by the defendant No.4 after receiving the consideration money on 04.04.1973. The learned Advocate also submits that the plaintiffs to the suit who are the opposite-parties of this revisional application, by sufficient evidence has been able to discharge their onus in proving their respective case that the defendant Nos. 1-3 after taking earnest money of Tk. 1550/- pursuant an oral agreement for sale in favour of the plaintiffs entered in to a contract but for want of income tax clearance certificate they could not execute and register a sale deed and subsequently when they denied to execute and register the deed the plaintiffs filed the original suit for specific performance of contract. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the appellate court below during disposal of the appeal considering all the facts and circumstance of the case including the evidence adduced from the sides of the respective parties reversed the judgment and decree of the trial court and decreed the suit which can't be interfered with by this court. 

 13. It has been contended from the side of the defendant-petitioners that the pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No.145 of 1973 which was filed by them against the kabla deed dated 04.04.1973 executed by the defendant No.4 in favour of the plaintiffs is the reason for which the plaintiffs instituted the suit for specific performance of contract to frustrate the statutory right of the defendants to have an order of pre-emption in respect of the kabla dated 04.04.1973 marked as exhibit-2 on a concocted story of oral contract. In this regard the teamed trial court assessing the evidence on records believed the case of the defendants and disbelieving the case of the plaintiffs dismissed the suit holding that the case of the plaintiffs is nothing but a cock-and-bull story. Subsequently; the lower appellate court hearing the appeal reversed the judgment on the ground that the plaintiff’s case of oral contract is proved but it is curious to note that in the content of the judgment the learned appellate court utterly failed to state as to how the plaintiff's case is proved and also failed to assess the evidence on records in its true perspective. 

 15. Scanning the evidence adduced from the sides of the parties it is noticed that among the plaintiff's 4(four) witnesses the witness No.1 is the plaintiff No.2 & this witness in his testimony expressed his inability to remember the date of talk of agreement i.e. the oral contract. The plaintiff No.2 states that for the first time the talk of sale was held in his residence & one Suruj Miah was present there and in the subsequent talk none was present & no date was fixed for execution of the kabla deed. The plaintiff's witness No.2 is the alleged presence of the First talk. This witness in his testimony states that the plaintiffs were tenant under the defendants and after the talk of sale due to liberation movement the kabla deed could not be executed and registered. The stamp was purchased but no writing was held & this witness was present at the time of 3rd talk when the consideration amount was settled. The witness No.3 Osman Khan is a hear-say witness of the case. The last witness No.4 Rukkini Suthrodhar it a carpenter who only repaired the standing but situated in the suit premises, Vis-à-vis; the only witness on behalf of the defendant-petitioners is one Mukul Chandra Das, son of late Bindu Bihari Das. This witness states in support of defendant's case.
